sources.title: Upinder Singh: Kings, Brāhmaṇas and Temples in Orissa, AD 300 to 1147
sources.note: Specialist epigraphic history used only for the overview: regional polities, royal grants, religious institutions and the archive’s elite bias.

sources.title: Dineshwar Singh: The History of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty, circa 1038 to 1238 AD
sources.note: Doctoral history used for Vajrahasta, Rajaraja, Chodaganga, Chola wars, Trikalinga and the dynasty’s expansion beyond 1100.

sources.title: Upinder Singh: Kings, Brāhmaṇas, and Temples in Orissa, full thesis scan
sources.note: Full scholarly study used for inscription find-spots, Kalinganagara grants, land endowments, political integration and evidence limits.

sources.title: Odisha State Museum: Copper Plate Grants of the Bhaumakara Period
sources.note: Official museum catalogue used for named Bhauma-Kara royal charters, their genealogies, ruling women and the surviving copper-plate archive.

sources.title: Devika Rangachari: From Obscurity to Light, Women in Early Medieval Orissa
sources.note: Specialist monograph used for royal and non-royal women, female rulers, donors, marriage, gendered evidence and changing dynasties.

sources.title: DHARMA: Chaudwār Plates of Mahābhavagupta Dharmakandarpa, Year 31
sources.note: Digital critical edition and translation used for Somavamshi titles, officials, villages, water-and-land clauses, learning, scribes and date cautions.

sources.title: DHARMA: Kelga Plates of Someśvaradeva, Year 1
sources.note: Digital primary edition used for Somavamshi succession language, Suvarnapura, Kosala, Uddyota Kesari and Trikalinga titulature.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica IX: Madras Museum Plates of Vajrahasta III
sources.note: Official epigraphic edition used for Vajrahasta’s 1038 to 1070 reign, Kalinganagara, five hundred Brahmana recipients and the 1062 grant.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Arasavalli Plates of Vajrahasta III, Śaka 982
sources.note: Epigraphia Indica edition used for the 1060 plates, eastern Nagari script, Sanskrit text, named women, kin groups, village shares and written sample.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Arasavalli Plates, grant terms and recipients
sources.note: Continuation of the official Epigraphia Indica edition used for the grant date, Kalinganagara issue place, named ministerial family, Kayastha and Sudra recipients, village divisions and shares.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica XI: Narasapatam Plates of Vajrahasta III
sources.note: Primary charter edition used for Dantapura, land, officers, Vamsadhara geography and the earliest dated grant of Vajrahasta III.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica XXIII: Ganjam Copper Plates of Vajrahasta III
sources.note: Primary charter edition used for genealogy, Sanskrit prose and verse, administrative transactions, land purchase and charter formulae.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica XXXI: Peddabammidi Plates of Vajrahasta III
sources.note: Primary edition used for Srikakulam provenance, Kalinganagara, Trikalinga claims, royal emblems and a military-service recipient.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica XXXIII: Chikkalavalasa Plates and Rajaraja I parallels
sources.note: Primary edition used for Vajrahasta’s charter series, Rajaraja I succession, repeated praise language and Srikakulam find context.

sources.title: Government Museum Chennai: Catalogue of Copper Plate Grants
sources.note: Official museum catalogue used for Eastern Ganga seals, scripts, grants and Chodaganga’s post-interval 1118 Utkala record.

sources.title: South Indian Inscriptions III: Inscriptions of Kulottunga Chola I
sources.note: Official inscription series used cautiously for Chola claims to Kalinga campaigns in 1095 to 1096 during Chodaganga’s reign.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Ancient India: The Kalinga War of Kulottunga I
sources.note: Scholarly ASI journal scan used to compare inscriptions with court poetry and to keep disputed Chola campaign sequences explicit.

sources.title: Subrata Kumar Acharya: Kings, Brāhmaṇas and Collective Land Grants in Early Medieval Odisha
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study used for collective grants, Brahmana beneficiaries, political authority and the limits of charter evidence for cultivators.

sources.title: Subrata Kumar Acharya: Aksasalika, Aksasalin, and Suvarnakara as Engravers of Copper Plate Charters of Odisha
sources.note: University repository study used for composers, engravers and specialized documentary labor in seventh- to eleventh-century Odisha.

sources.title: CBSE Knowledge Traditions: Early and Classical Indian Architecture
sources.note: Official educational survey used for tenth- and eleventh-century Muktesvara, Rajarani and Lingaraja and mature Kalinga temple forms.

sources.title: Cornell Digital Collections: Brahmesvara Temple
sources.note: University visual archive used for the Somavamshi temple’s late eleventh-century date, location and architectural attribution.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Buddhist Monuments at Ratnagiri
sources.note: Official excavation monograph used for monastery plans, cells, shrines, sealings and rebuilding after the eleventh century.

sources.title: Umakanta Mishra: Stūpa as Dharmadhātu and Maṇḍala at Udayagiri, Odisha
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study used for ninth- to tenth-century mandala stupas, dharanis, new monastery identity and Buddhist ritual change.

sources.title: The Creative South: Circulation of Buddhist Maṇḍalas in Maritime Asia
sources.note: Cambridge chapter used for Odisha’s eighth- to eleventh-century Buddhist iconographic programs and wider maritime religious connections.

sources.title: Odisha Archaeology: Manikapatna, An Excavation Report
sources.note: Official excavation report used for a long-lived coastal settlement, port evidence, pottery, fish bones, beads, tools and chronological limits.

sources.title: National Institute of Oceanography: Maritime archaeological explorations around Chilika Lake
sources.note: Government research repository copy of a peer-reviewed study used for Manikapatna ornaments, ceramics, maritime finds, reported ring wells and the evidential limits of surface and multi-period material.

sources.title: Trade and Traders in Early Medieval Odisha
sources.note: University research used for merchant groups, inscriptions, turquoise glazed ware, cowries and Bay of Bengal exchange evidence.

sources.title: Geochemical Provenance of an Indo-Arabian Stone Anchor from Manikapatna
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open-access archaeology used for medieval anchoring technology, stone provenance and caution about broad dating.

sources.title: National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities: Odisha gamesmen catalogue results
sources.note: Official inventory used only to document gamesmen from Odisha sites while emphasizing that entries lack a secure 900 to 1100 association.

sources.title: UNESCO Tentative List: Ekamra Kshetra, the Temple City of Bhubaneswar
sources.note: UNESCO dossier used for historic temple-town water tanks, ponds, sandstone monuments and the long, multi-dynastic landscape.

proposedOverrides.summary: The atlas label ends at 1100, but its two geometries represent no single continuous polity and Eastern Ganga expansion continued afterward.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id is kalinga-900, displayed Kalinga and indexed circa 900 to 1100 CE; it is separate from early kalinga, somvamsis, orissa, orissa-1279 and western-gangas.
Initial coverage records two border files and observed intervals 900 to 1000 and 1000 to 1100, an imported summary, and no card or override.
The exact target is absent at 800, present once at 900 and 1000, and absent at the indexed 1100 endpoint and later 1200 and 1279 seams.
The 900 target is one Polygon, one part, one ring and fourteen positions; bounds are [80.95940959409597,16.645832282689426,84.24624246242462,19.237972318851135].
The 900 raw coordinate SHA-256 is f7d449e162d6259213e317fdaabe9e011911742730251f461ca0d183f5d4ffea; canonical hash is a6c036195eef7d63f20cc6658c25a362d28cf4db7f0433bd5508b681008e38ce.
The 1000 target is one Polygon, one part, one ring and twenty-six positions; bounds are [77.65457654576545,14.328691991168512,83.68823688236881,20.666406280168005].
The 1000 raw coordinate SHA-256 is a386b56bd440267e70bbe1607e9049a1f99a46408146153b54d3dd14bf0c6469; canonical hash is 9874c606f329ccfb1b7a9ca5da25812ef8e0456c79115bdb0c1bb50663edcf13.

The 900 polygon contains Srikakulam, Simhachalam and Rajamahendravaram but excludes Mukhalingam and all tested core-Odisha places; the 1000 polygon instead contains Simhachalam, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram and Bastar.

At 900 Mukhalingam is in somvamsis and core Odisha in palas; at 1000 Mukhalingam and Srikakulam are in orissa while core Odisha remains in palas. These are display assignments, not primary-source borders.
The closest historical reading is a southern-Kalinga early Eastern Ganga context for 900 and a seriously distorted Andhra-Vengi composite for 1000; neither supports one continuous Kalinga empire.
Every coordinate describes imported display geometry only; it does not establish ethnicity, language, modern claims or exclusive medieval sovereignty.
